 EG-3DVG: Expression and Geometry Aware Grounding Decoder for 3D Visual
                             Grounding

     GwangWook Park1 Hyo-Jun Lee2 Jong-Hyeon Baek1 Hanul Kim3 Yeong Jun Koh1∗
               1
                 Chungnam National University 2 Kangwon National University
                     3
                       Seoul National University of Science and Technology
             ccocco0609@o.cnu.ac.kr, gywns6298@kangwon.ac.kr, jonghyeon9587@o.cnu.ac.kr
                                       hukim@seoultech.ac.kr, yjkoh@cnu.ac.kr



                            Abstract

Despite recent progress in 3D visual grounding, existing
methods still struggle with three core challenges: 1) cross-
modal misalignment that prevents textual cues from being
reliably delivered to visual representations, 2) intra-class
confusion arising from insufficient understanding of fine-
grained expression cues, and 3) geometric reasoning errors
caused by inaccurate aggregation of spatially relevant vi-
sual features. We propose EG-3DVG, a unified framework
that addresses these issues through an expression and ge-
ometry aware grounding decoder. The decoder integrates
two complementary attention modules—position-guided ex-
pression cross-attention (PECA) for reliable text–vision
alignment and geometry-aware masked attention (GMA) for
selective aggregation of geometry-consistent visual cues. To
further distinguish semantically similar instances, we intro-
duce expression-aware contrastive learning (ECL), which                Figure 1. Illustration of failure examples on ScanRefer [6]: (a)
strengthens the alignment between the target object token              cross-modal misalignment, (b) intra-category confusion, and (c)
                                                                       geometric reasoning error.
and expression-relevant words. Extensive experiments on
ScanRefer and SR3D/NR3D demonstrate that EG-3DVG
achieves state-of-the-art performance in both 3D bound-                target object within a 3D point cloud scene based on a tex-
ing box localization and mask prediction, validating the               tual description that depicts the object’s attributes, such as
effectiveness of our geometry- and expression-aware de-                its appearance (e.g. ”blue”, ”red”), category (e.g. ”desk”,
sign. Code is available at https://github.com/                         ”chair”), and spatial relationships with other objects (e.g.
Gwan9Wook/EG3DVG.                                                      “next to the table”, “on the left of the sofa”).

Figure 2. Overview of EG-3DVG. In expression and geometry aware grounding decoder, position-guided expression cross-attention injects
positional information to each text tokens and geometry-aware masked attention incorporates geometric relationship into the attention
mechanism. Expression-aware contrastive learning encourages the selected visual token to align with expression-relevant words (e.g.
attribute, pronoun, relationship) from the text description while contrasting against other texts describing same-category distractors.

                                                                                       5. Conclusion
Table 4. Ablation study on different combinations of PECA,                             In this work, we presented EG-3DVG, a 3D visual ground-
GMA, and ECL on ScanRefer.                                                             ing framework that addresses three major limitations: cross-
                                                                                       modal misalignment, intra-class confusion, and geometric
to 0.75m, corresponding to the average object size in Scan-                            reasoning errors. We introduced an expression and ge-
Refer. This approach simply aggregates information from                                ometry aware grounding decoder that integrates two com-
nearby tokens without considering their geometric relation-                            plementary modules, PECA and GMA, to achieve reliable
ships. Second, we directly project the geometric feature G                             text–vision alignment and geometry-consistent feature ag-
into a softened attention map through an MLP followed by                               gregation. In addition, we proposed an expression-aware
a sigmoid function. This method excludes text tokens from                              contrastive learning to enhance the model’s ability to distin-
the attention mask generation, leading to the aggregation of                           guish semantically similar instances based on fine-grained
spatially close but expression-irrelevant visual features. In                          expression cues. Experimental results on ScanRefer and
contrast, the proposed GMA jointly explores geometric and                              SR3D/NR3D demonstrate that EG-3DVG achieves state-of-
textual features for attention mask, consistently achieving                            the-art performance on both 3D bounding box localization
the highest 3DREC and 3DRES performance.                                               and mask prediction.
